CheckTitle: Jenkins controllers are served over HTTPS
Description: This check verifies that the Jenkins root URL uses `https`, so session cookies, API tokens and build output are encrypted in transit between users and the controller.
Risk: Over plain HTTP, the Jenkins **session cookie and API token travel in cleartext** and can be captured by anyone positioned on the network path, including on a shared office or VPN segment. Because a captured administrator session grants script console access, this escalates directly to code execution on every build agent.

Code.Other:
1. Terminate TLS at a reverse proxy (nginx, Apache, or a cloud load balancer) in front of Jenkins, or configure the built-in Jetty listener with a keystore
2. Redirect all HTTP traffic to HTTPS at the proxy
3. Go to **Manage Jenkins > System** and set the **Jenkins URL** to the `https://` address
4. Enable HSTS at the proxy
5. Bind the Jenkins HTTP listener to `127.0.0.1` so it is reachable only through the proxy
Code.Terraform:
# Jenkins Configuration as Code (jenkins.yaml)
unclassified:
  location:
    url: "https://jenkins.example.com/"
    adminAddress: "platform@example.com"

Recommendation.Text: Serve Jenkins over HTTPS with a valid certificate, redirect HTTP to HTTPS, set the Jenkins URL to the https address, and bind the plain HTTP listener to localhost only.
